title: ApexLedger POC scoping - workload & benchmarks
summary: POC scoping to validate Redwood Dedicated for ApexLedger payments workflows. Focus: model sizing, target QPS and concurrency, token distributions for authorization and reconciliation flows, benchmark plan and timeline. Customer needs p95 latency targets and deterministic cost estimates; security questions (VPC, KMS, audit logs) to be answered in follow-up. Agreed next step: Redwood to run small synthetic benchmark and share spreadsheet + pricing; customer to provide sample traffic profile and golden prompts.
next_steps: Redwood: run 3-model bench (alpaca-like, redwood-v2-small, quantized 4-bit) with provided sample - due 2025-11-25
ApexLedger: share 2 weeks of redacted request logs and golden prompts - due 2025-11-20
Schedule deep-dive demo of Dedicated infra with security team - tentative 2025-11-27
action_items: Alice Morgan - send benchmark template and pricing worksheet - 2025-11-19
Priya Singh - upload redacted traffic sample and golden prompts - 2025-11-20
Diego Ramos - prepare workload modeling spreadsheet and initial capacity plan - 2025-11-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 60m
Attendees: Alice Morgan (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Taylor Chen (Redwood Eng Ops); Priya Singh (ApexLedger Head of ML), Markus Lee (CTO), Jared Cole (SRE), Lena Ortiz (Product)

Summary (auto): POC to validate Redwood Dedicated for payment ops; primary metrics: p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, model accuracy vs oracle prompts.

00:00 - Alice Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'll kick off quickly, uh, we're here to scope the POC around workload modeling and benchmarks for the payment flows you mentioned in the form
00:18 - Priya Singh: thanks alice, we wanna make sure we model the auth and reconciliation flows separately, they look very different, auth is short and latency-sensitive, recon is long and throughput-y, and there's also a nightly batch ingestion job
00:35 - Diego Ramos: yeah that matches what we typically see; can you give ballpark numbers for QPS and typical token sizes for each flow? even rough percentiles help
00:50 - Markus Lee: sure, for auth peak QPS is about 80 rps globally, normally steady 20 rps, 95th bursts up to 120 for 30-60s during morning windows; payloads are tiny, input tokens ~30-80, outputs 20-40, want p95 <250ms ideally
01:12 - Priya Singh: reconciliation is different — it's async, we run many concurrent jobs, concurrency around 300 workers hitting the model but per-job QPS is low, typical inputs 500-1,500 tokens, outputs 800-2,000, and latency tolerances are higher (p95 <3s)
01:34 - Jared Cole: and there's a third flow, dashboard summarization, which is interactive for ops, concurrency maybe 40, inputs 120 tokens, outputs 400 tokens, p95 <600ms preferred
01:50 - Diego Ramos: ok so auth: low tokens, high QPS, strict p95; recon: high tokens, high concurrency but batchy; dashboard: medium tokens and latency. For POC we'll need sample distributions not just averages — 50/90/99 percentiles for tokens and qps windows
02:18 - Lena Ortiz: on success criteria — we want to be able to project unit economics for 3 months. If we can't confidently estimate cost per million tokens for peak vs baseline we can't sell this internally
02:35 - Alice Morgan: understood. Typical Redwood POC success criteria we recommend: 1) meet latency SLOs for auth at p95, 2) reconciliation throughput within cost target per job, 3) no functional regressions on golden prompts, 4) security controls validated (VPC + KMS + audit logs).
02:57 - Priya Singh: yes, and add accuracy threshold — our golden set needs >95% match to incumbent model for reconciliation decisions else manual intervention skyrockets
03:12 - Markus Lee: security is non-negotiable. We need VPC peering or Private deployment, KMS for keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Do you have SOC 2 cert?
03:29 - Alice Morgan: we do have SOC 2, and our Private/Dedicated offer supports customer-managed KMS and audit forwarding. I'll attach the security overview. 
03:40 - Jared Cole: okay good. On capacity, are you configuring autoscaling for Dedicated? we don't want noisy neighbors affecting auth p95
03:52 - Diego Ramos: yes Dedicated pools are isolated; autoscaler configs can be tuned for warm GPUs, pre-warmed nodes for auth. For the auth path we recommend a small fleet of low-latency short-context models pinned to a GPU class with pre-warm. For reconciliation we use batching and quantized models for cost.
04:15 - Priya Singh: can you give concrete qps->instance sizing example? like if we have sustained 20 rps and peak 120, what do we need?
04:24 - Diego Ramos: rough example: with our redwood-v2-small baseline (gpt-like), an instance with A100-equivalent can handle ~200 tokens/s for generation at single-concurrency low-latency mode. For auth (avg tokens 60 roundtrip) that's roughly 3-4 rps per GPU if latency optimized; but we use multi-tenant batching and efficient kernels so practical throughput higher. We usually model at request-level: tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * concurrency = tokens/sec capacity. We'll deliver a modeling spreadsheet with conservative, nominal, and optimistic estimates
05:00 - Markus Lee: hmm those numbers imply we need a few dedicated GPUs just for auth? that's concerning for cost
05:07 - Alice Morgan: that's why we propose hybrid routing: auth to a low-latency hosted tier or dedicated pinned small model; Redwood can route auth to a higher-cost low-latency pool and recon to cost-optimized pool, keeping p95 guarantees. We'll show cost tradeoffs in the pricing sheet
05:28 - Priya Singh: about token distribution, we can share a 2-week sample. It will include request timestamps, input token counts, output token counts, and a label for flow type. Is that enough?
05:40 - Diego Ramos: perfect. Also include golden prompts and expected outputs for a sample of reconciliation runs so we can validate quality.
05:50 - Priya Singh: yes we'll redact pii and send by tomorrow. 
06:00 - Alice Morgan: great. For benchmarks we propose three tests: 1) auth latency sweep (single request, p95 measurement at target QPS), 2) recon throughput (multi-worker, long context), 3) nightly batch cost run (embedding + summarize). We'll run each across 3 model variants and quantization levels and capture token-level cost and p95 latency
06:28 - Jared Cole: for recon the model may need long context support — do you support kv cache and long-attn? we have docs up to 8k tokens and sometimes 16k on big jobs
06:40 - Diego Ramos: yes runtime supports KV cache and 32k in some binaries; there are performance tradeoffs, but for recon we'd likely chunk inputs or use long-seq optimized kernels. We'll record memory and latency metrics per sequence length in the spreadsheet
06:58 - Markus Lee: what's the timeline for running these? we need results before our budget meeting on Dec 10th
07:06 - Alice Morgan: target is to run initial synthetic benchmarks within 1 week (by Nov 25), then a real-data run after we get your logs (by Dec 2), and final report by Dec 8 to give you time before Dec 10 meeting
07:22 - Priya Singh: tight but doable. Who owns data handling during the POC? do you pull data into Redwood cloud or can we keep it in our VPC?
07:34 - Diego Ramos: for Dedicated we can do either: option A - bring redacted logs to our bench in staging hosted env; option B - deploy Private connector so logs never leave your VPC. We'll include both options in the plan and cost the connector work separately
07:52 - Lena Ortiz: okay we prefer VPC option for security reasons; will need SOW for Private connector work and estimated eng hours
07:58 - Alice Morgan: noted, we'll include SOW estimates.
08:06 - Markus Lee: another question — how do you handle model fallbacks and graceful degradation? if the Dedicated pool is saturated during a morning spike we need a fallback route to hosted model in another region
08:20 - Diego Ramos: Redwood supports routing policies: fallback to compatible model variants or another region with burst capacity; we can configure per-route SLOs and automatic fallback thresholds. We'll show a routing policy example in the sheet
08:35 - Priya Singh: on quality: our golden prompts include reconciliation edge cases; if the model drifts we need regression alerts tied to evals. Do you support automated eval runs?
08:46 - Alice Morgan: yes Optimize includes eval hooks and can run prompt-based suites nightly, with regression alerts and comparisons across model versions. We'll demo that in the follow-up session
08:58 - Jared Cole: we also need logging and observability — per-token cost, latency breakdown, trace ids forwarded to our tracer
09:08 - Diego Ramos: we emit per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns, and can forward logs to your SIEM. For Private we can also integrate with on-prem ELK or Splunk
09:22 - Priya Singh: circling back to workload modeling — what inputs do you need from us? you mentioned percentiles and golden prompts
09:30 - Diego Ramos: yes: 1) 2 weeks of redacted request logs with timestamps and token counts, 2) golden prompts and expected outputs for 100 examples per flow, 3) peak window definitions and any planned traffic growth assumptions, 4) security constraints (VPC, KMS)
09:52 - Priya Singh: we'll get that to you by EOD tomorrow, except the golden prompts need internal review but we'll try to meet 11/20
10:00 - Alice Morgan: great. On the modeling spreadsheet we'll show three scenarios: conservative (no batching, higher latency), nominal (expected batching), and optimistic (aggressive batching/quantization). We'll include assumed batching windows, cold-start penalties, and tail-latency buffers
10:22 - Markus Lee: curious about batching — how do you preserve auth latency if you batch? won't that increase p95 dramatically?
10:31 - Diego Ramos: batching is disabled for auth path; we rely on kernel-level optimizations, small context models and pre-warmed instances. For recon we enable batching aggressively — that's where most cost savings are. Also prefix/KV caching helps when many requests share context
10:50 - Priya Singh: caching seems useful for dashboard and some recon jobs that repeat similar prompts
10:56 - Alice Morgan: exactly. We'll instrument cache hit ratios in the POC and show cost delta.
11:03 - Lena Ortiz: on pricing — will you give committed pricing for Dedicated during POC or just estimates?
11:10 - Alice Morgan: POC pricing is estimates; if you go to Dedicated with a commit we can provide reserved capacity pricing and monthly SKUs. We'll show both options in the proposal
11:23 - Jared Cole: one more thing — SLA and incident response; will you provide phone-on-call for production switchover?
11:31 - Alice Morgan: enterprise packages include 24/7 support with escalation paths; we'll include recommended support tier for your projected traffic
11:39 - Priya Singh: ok let's recap next steps
11:42 - Alice Morgan: recap: Redwood runs initial synthetic bench by 11/25; ApexLedger shares redacted logs and golden prompts by 11/20; Redwood sends workload modeling spreadsheet and draft SOW for Private connector by 11/19; schedule security deep-dive with your security team for week of 11/27.
12:05 - Markus Lee: that sounds good. thanks everyone.
12:10 - Alice Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and the sheet. Bye.

Notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cache" appears in raw text), small overlaps/crosstalk around 05:00 and 11:30.
